A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CaP-X study and contain readable main text, figures, tables, and appendices. Relocated and renumbered content can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original robot-manipulation evaluations, component ablations, and simulation and real-robot post-training results, including Figures 3–8, Table 4, and appendix analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds a computational timing study in Appendix K.2 and Table 9.

M1.justification: The control interfaces, visual differencing, skill synthesis, ensemble procedure, and GRPO post-training remain unchanged. Specifying the rollout pool and synthesis model clarifies the existing implementation; it does not establish a revised method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same seven core Robosuite tasks, 30 LIBERO-PRO tasks, two BEHAVIOR tasks, and real-robot demonstrations. The new timing study reuses cube stacking. The added breakdown of the 187-task release does not expand evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: The evaluated frontier models, human references, Qwen baseline, and OpenVLA, π0, and π0.5 comparisons are retained. Appendix K.2 cites existing VLA latency figures for context rather than introducing newly evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Appendix K.2 introduces a timing protocol: Gemini-3-Pro cube stacking over 20 trials, measuring code-generation and total trial time across S1, S2, S3, M1, and M3 with matched hardware and perception/control stacks. Existing success-rate evaluation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix K.2 adds wall-clock computational-cost analysis across tiers, complementing the existing turn/token analyses. Existing ablations, robustness evaluations, and case studies are retained. The suggested VDM-backbone ablation in K.3 is not performed.

E5.justification: Existing trial counts and plotted uncertainty displays are unchanged. Table 9 extends mean-over-trials reporting to a new timing sample without adding seed information, uncertainty estimates, significance tests, or a new statistical reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 9 newly reports timing results, including code-generation/total trial times of 6.8/12.9 seconds for S1 and 15.8/113.6 seconds for M3. Existing success rates, ablation results, and appendix findings are unchanged. The human reference of 88.5% already appeared in v1 Figure 1.

T1.justification: No formal assumptions, mathematical definitions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised. Expanded explanations of environment turns and shared code-action interfaces are conceptual clarifications.

C1.justification: The abstract qualifies human-level reliability as near human-level and replaces the minimal sim-to-real gap claim with transfer through a shared code-action interface. Section 5 confines the robustness statement to the demonstrated tasks. The four principal contributions remain the same.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly interprets the human baseline as extensively refined offline code, distinguishes per-task from per-action latency, and explains the VDM-backbone choice. Sim-to-real interpretation emphasizes shared tools and demonstrated tasks. Existing contact-rich limitations are retained in the relocated Future Works appendix.

D1.justification: Section 4 specifies pooling successful S3 rollouts across all 12 models and seven tasks and using Gemini-3-Pro for skill synthesis. Appendix K documents the seven author-experts, their experience and development effort, and the benchmark-wide VDM backbone. These supplement the retained APIs, prompts, and code listings.

R1.justification: Section 6 substantially contracts the research context, removing discussions and citations covering multi-robot coordination, scene-graph planning, software-agent platforms, and several code-RL systems, including RoCo, SayPlan, OpenHands, and CodeRL. ReTool is added. The central positioning around low-level primitives and direct RLVR remains.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten, related work is substantially condensed, and several methodological explanations are revised. Future Works moves from Section 7 to Appendix A, existing appendices are renumbered, and Appendix K is added. Author and publication information also changes.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 9, expands the Table 1 caption, adjusts figure placement, and uses higher-resolution versions of Figures 1, 19, and 23–26 with unchanged content. The existing visual organization and table structures otherwise remain substantially intact.

improvement.justification: v2 improves transparency about the human baseline and skill-library construction, qualifies the sim-to-real claim, and adds useful timing evidence. These gains improve interpretation and reproducibility without changing the main experimental findings. Benefits are limited by timing coverage of one task and selected tiers, while the shortened related-work section sacrifices breadth.
